PROCUREMENT

Design-and-Execution Interfaces: Questions to Ask Before Appointment

Integrated delivery still needs explicit design ownership and review routes.

In this insight

Do not let a label replace a scopeDefine the review pathwayCoordinate temporary and permanent designAgree how changes are managedFor your project discussionDiscuss a project ↗

Educational overview · Project-specific design and execution require qualified review.

Do not let a label replace a scope

Terms such as integrated solution or design and execution can cover different arrangements. Ask which design activities are included, who performs them and who retains responsibility for interfaces with other structures or packages. An attractive description should be translated into named deliverables and obligations. This helps the client understand what is actually being purchased and what remains with its own consultants.

Define the review pathway

Identify required checks, reviews and approvals, including any independent review specified for the project. State the expected inputs and submission sequence. Distinguish a review process from an endorsement or guarantee by an institution. The contract should describe the actual arrangement rather than imply that a future review has already occurred.

Coordinate temporary and permanent design

Ground engineering can interact with both temporary support and the completed structure. Make the boundary between those responsibilities explicit. Ask how design assumptions will be shared and how conflicts will be resolved. Where the same physical element serves more than one role, the project needs a coordinated brief rather than parallel designs based on different interpretations.

Agree how changes are managed

Set a process for design queries, revised inputs and proposed alternatives. Record technical approval and commercial impact separately but link them in the change register. The delivery team should know which documents are authorised and what remains under review. Clear ownership allows an integrated package to work as intended without assuming that integration eliminates the need for disciplined coordination.

For your project discussion

Use these questions to structure a conversation with the project’s qualified design and delivery team. This article is general procurement guidance, not a site-specific design, method statement or compliance assessment. The cited international resources provide background; applicable local requirements and the approved project documents govern the work.

Take this into your next conversation

  • Name the included design deliverables.
  • Define checks and approvals accurately.
  • Coordinate temporary and permanent responsibilities.

References & further reading

  • Further reading: FHWA — Earth retaining structures guidance

International references provide technical context; applicable local requirements and the project engineer’s decisions govern the actual works.
